body.statement:
At \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), put
\[
B_\star=B_{\eta,h}\{x_\star(\eta,h)\},
\qquad s_\star=s_1(B_\star),
\]
and let \(u_\star,v_\star\in\mathbb R^2\) be unit left and right singular vectors for \(s_\star\), with first coordinates \(u_{\star,1}\) and \(v_{\star,1}\).  The top singular value is simple and \(s_\star>c^{1/4}\).  Define
\[
\ell_c(s)=\frac{s^4-c}{s^2(s^2+c)},
\qquad
r_c(s)=\frac{s^4-c}{s^2(s^2+1)},
\]
and
\[
a_D(\eta,h)=\sqrt{pq}
\left\{1-\ell_c(s_\star)u_{\star,1}^2\right\}^{1/2}
\left\{1-r_c(s_\star)v_{\star,1}^2\right\}^{1/2}>0.
\]
For every compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), uniformly over \((\eta,h)\in\mathcal K\),
\[
\frac{\|\widetilde D\|_F}{\sqrt{NT}}\xrightarrow{p}a_D(\eta,h),
\qquad
\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma,
\qquad
\Pr\{\operatorname{ATT}_{NT}\in\mathrm{CI}_F\}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus conventional full-sample IFE Wald coverage is strictly below \(1-\alpha\), indeed asymptotically zero, throughout compact subsets of the absorption phase.  This phase is relatively open and is nonempty exactly when
\[
\overline h>\min_{\eta\in\mathcal E_{\mathrm{loc}}}h_{\mathrm{crit}}(\eta).
\]
All conclusions concern only the bounded experiment \(h=\theta/\sigma\in[-\overline h,\overline h]\).
body.justification: Strictly beyond the same threshold, the order-\(m^{-1/2}\) absorption bias dominates an order-\(m^{-1}\) conventional standard error.
body.gap: Generic weak-factor results do not provide this rank-one treatment overlap formula or its exact nonempty phase.
body.consumer: It converts the phase law into uniform zero coverage for conventional full-sample IFE Wald inference on every compact absorbed subregion.
body.proof_tex:
Fix a compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\).  By the exact phase theorem, every point in \(\mathcal K\) is strictly supercritical and
\(\widehat x_F\to x_\star\) uniformly.  In the sign-rotated two-by-two representation used by the global singleton theorem, the selected coordinate satisfies
\(0<z_\star<z_0\), while the other three matrix entries are strictly positive.  The off-diagonal entry of the corresponding two-by-two left Gram matrix is therefore strictly positive.  Its two eigenvalues are distinct, so \(s_\star\) is simple.  Equation (19) and the strict supercritical selection rule also give \(s_\star>c^{1/4}\).  Compactness supplies uniform gaps both from the spectral edge and from the second population singular value.

Let \(e_1,f_1\) be the treatment-support vectors in (2).  The strong-block equations (1)--(6), evaluated at \(\widehat x_F\), show that the first \(r\) selected left and right singular spaces converge to \(U_0\) and \(V_0\).  The additional selected singular pair is the leading outlier pair generated by
\(Z_{22}+P_{x_\star}\), because replacing \(\widehat x_F\) by \(x_\star\) changes the perturbation by \(o_p(1)\) in operator norm.  For \(c\leq1\), the cited singular-vector-overlap theorem gives
\[
|\langle\widehat u,e_1\rangle|^2
\xrightarrow{p}\ell_c(s_\star)u_{\star,1}^2,
\qquad
|\langle\widehat v,f_1\rangle|^2
\xrightarrow{p}r_c(s_\star)v_{\star,1}^2. \tag{21}
\]
The factors \(u_{\star,1}^2\) and \(v_{\star,1}^2\) appear because the cited theorem also makes projections on the distinct population singular-vector direction vanish.  When \(c>1\), apply that theorem to
\(c^{-1/2}(Z_{22}+P_{x_\star})^{\top}\).  Its aspect ratio is \(1/c\), its spike is \(s_\star/\sqrt c\), and its left and right vectors are interchanged.  Algebra gives
\[
\frac{s_\star^4/c^2-1/c}
{(s_\star^2/c)(s_\star^2/c+1/c)}
=\frac{s_\star^4-c}{s_\star^2(s_\star^2+1)}=r_c(s_\star),
\]
\[
\frac{s_\star^4/c^2-1/c}
{(s_\star^2/c)(s_\star^2/c+1)}
=\frac{s_\star^4-c}{s_\star^2(s_\star^2+c)}=\ell_c(s_\star),
\]
so (21) holds for every \(c>0\).  Edge and simplicity separation make the convergence uniform on \(\mathcal K\).

Since \(D=\sqrt{n_1t_1}\,e_1f_1^{\top}\), and since
\(e_1\perp U_0\) and \(f_1\perp V_0\),
\[
\frac{\|\widetilde D\|_F}{\sqrt{NT}}
=\sqrt{p_Nq_T}\,
\|(I-P_{\widehat U})e_1\|_2
\|(I-P_{\widehat V})f_1\|_2. \tag{22}
\]
Substitution of (21) into (22), followed by \(p_N\to p\) and \(q_T\to q\), proves the displayed formula for \(a_D\).  For every finite
\(s>c^{1/4}\), direct subtraction from one gives
\[
0<\ell_c(s)<1,
\qquad
0<r_c(s)<1. \tag{23}
\]
Thus both factors defining \(a_D\) are strictly positive even when a first population singular-vector coordinate has absolute value one.  Continuity and compactness give a common positive lower bound on \(\mathcal K\).

We next prove variance consistency.  The absorption law gives
\(\widehat\beta_F-\gamma=O_p(m^{-1/2})\).  With
\[
R_{NT}=H-(\widehat\beta_F-\gamma)D,
\]
the bounded-score assumptions, the aspect envelope, and the share envelope give
\(\operatorname{rank}(R_{NT})\leq2\) and \(\|R_{NT}\|_F=O_p(\sqrt T)\).  Choosing
\(L=\Lambda F^{\top}\), which has rank at most \(r+1\), in the profiled residual problem yields
\[
\|Y-\widehat\beta_FD-\widehat L_F\|_F^2
\leq\|E+R_{NT}\|_F^2
=\|E\|_F^2+o_p(NT), \tag{24}
\]
where the last step follows from
\(2\|E\|_F\|R_{NT}\|_F+\|R_{NT}\|_F^2=o_p(NT)\).

For the reverse bound, write
\[
Y-\widehat\beta_FD-\widehat L_F=E-K_{NT},
\qquad
K_{NT}=\widehat L_F-(\Lambda F^{\top}+R_{NT}).
\]
Then \(\operatorname{rank}(K_{NT})\leq2r+3\).  The singular-value variational characterization of best fixed-rank approximation therefore gives
\[
\|Y-\widehat\beta_FD-\widehat L_F\|_F^2
\geq\|E\|_F^2-\sum_{j=1}^{2r+3}s_j(E)^2. \tag{25}
\]
The Gaussian law of large numbers and the Gaussian operator-norm bound imply
\[
\frac{\|E\|_F^2}{NT}\xrightarrow{p}\sigma^2,
\qquad
\frac1{NT}\sum_{j=1}^{2r+3}s_j(E)^2
=O_p(N^{-1})=o_p(1). \tag{26}
\]
Equations (24)--(26) show that the residual sum of squares divided by \(NT\) converges to \(\sigma^2\).  Since \(r\) is fixed and the aspect ratio is bounded away from zero and infinity,
\(\nu_F/(NT)\to1\); the nonnegative-root convention then gives
\(\widehat\sigma_F\xrightarrow{p}\sigma\), uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).

Finally define
\[
b(\eta,h)=x_\star(\eta,h)-h\mu_a\mu_b.
\]
The exact phase classification makes \(b\) continuous and nonzero on
\(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\), so \(\inf_{\mathcal K}|b|>0\).  The absorption law gives
\[
\frac{\sqrt m(\widehat\beta_F-\operatorname{ATT}_{NT})}{\sigma}
\xrightarrow{p}b(\eta,h), \tag{27}
\]
whereas (22), variance consistency, and \(NT\asymp m^2\) give
\[
\frac{\sqrt m}{\sigma}
\frac{z_{1-\alpha/2}\widehat\sigma_F}{\|\widetilde D\|_F}
=O_p(m^{-1/2})\longrightarrow0. \tag{28}
\]
If the Wald interval contains the target, the absolute value on the left of (27) cannot exceed (28).  The positive uniform lower bound for \(|b|\) makes the probability of that event tend to zero uniformly on \(\mathcal K\).  The relative openness and the exact nonemptiness criterion for
\(\mathcal A_{\mathrm{abs}}\) were proved in the absorption theorem, completing the result.
